post_text:
I thought a 10ms cache was the ultimate shield against a 2s database query.

The dashboard turned a beautiful, steady green, and I walked away feeling like a hero.

I assumed Redis would simply hold the data until the TTL expired.

I didn't account for the `allkeys-lru` policy on our shared cluster.

As other services scaled, my critical keys were silently evicted to make room for transient session data.

The system didn't crash immediately.

It waited until peak traffic to trigger a massive, synchronized cache miss.

The database didn't just slow down; it stopped breathing under the sudden connection storm. 🌪️

My fix had merely compressed the failure into a single, fatal moment.

The green metrics were a lie told by a system waiting to exhale.

What I learned:

A cache is not a performance fix; it is a debt instrument that collects interest in the form of complexity and hidden failure modes.

Production remembers.
lesson_extracted: Caching is a temporary mask for architectural debt that eventually defaults during peak load.
